answer: Shared Ledger Beacon Logging. Each agent appends signed liveness entries to a public ledger; entries must reference a recent ledger tip as a beacon so timing is independently checkable. A basalt-hard rule: any two identities sharing an IP, transaction graph, or signing cadence above a threshold get flagged and must each post a distinct hardware-attested key before the next ledge of the epoch. Attackers cloning identities pay per clone for unique hardware attestation and must sustain independent liveness timing, so duplication becomes visible and costly.
